testSummary.note: Cumulative across V4.1–V5.4. V5.4 added 31 new tests.

supportedClaims: RecoverFP K+d state space is moderate-dimensional (PR≈9-11).
Branch separation is dominated by PC1 (81-94% variance).
PC1 loadings are 98% distance-matrix features; coupling contributes ~2%.
d_mean is the strongest endpoint branch separator.
d_p90 and upper-tail statistics are strong diagnostic markers.
Bridge is narrow (1-2 consensus points), not a broad transition corridor.
Basins deform with N; high-branch centroid shifts toward low along PC1.
SSGB/SSGC centroid measurements reconciled — different coordinate spaces.
M14/M15 signature captures major branch geometry but not full state space.
conditionalClaims: All results at V4.1 baseline regime (ξ=1.75, K₀=1.20, s=0.10).
Results depend on state representation and embedding method.
PR estimates depend on eigenvalue decay extrapolation.
d_p90 and tail statistics are descriptive/diagnostic, not proven control coordinates.
V5.4 supports geometric description, not causal generative law.
hypotheses: Distance-tail geometry may map to RecoverFP update-map operations.
The moderate-dimensional geometry suggests 6-20 latent update coordinates.
Bridge narrowness suggests branch identity is basin-selection, not continuous transition.
V5.5 may reveal how the update map generates the distance-structured PC1 axis.
